a novel mutation in a serine-threonise kinase receptor, BMPR1B, causes either brachydactyl type A2 or brachydactly type C/proximal symphalngism-like phenotype, and the mutation is located in the kinase domain.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional characterization of the novel R486Q BMPR1B mutation and the resulting clinical manifestations.
a better understanding of the molecular pathomechanism of brachydactylies and other limb malformations.
a novel mutation in the BMPR1b receptor gene, the clinical and genetic spectrum of the disease, and functional studies of the mutation.

the R486Q BMPR1B mutant is a gain-of-function mutation, resulting in a dominant-negative effect.

the R486Q BMPR1B mutation is associated with a BDC/SYMP-like phenotype, which is in line with its strong inhibitory effect on chondrogenesis in micromass cultures.
